title: error_report.submitted
description: A member of a tenant reported an error in one of its obligations (a wrong due date, a rule that should not apply, a wrong step or citation, or something else). The obligation service stores the report under row-level security and emits it with the description masked for personal identifiers (the kernel's mask_pii_in, the record patterns log lines and audit rows are masked with, cut to the description's limit), so the rulebook, which every tenant shares, never holds a tenant's personal data; the rulebook's group rulebook.error-reports masks it once more and turns it into a review item for the regulatory team. Producer: obligation. Consumers: rulebook.

report_id.description: The report, as the obligation service keys it; the rulebook's review item is idempotent on it and the decision names it.

obligation_id.description: The obligation the report is about.

business_id.description: The business the obligation belongs to.

rule_version_id.description: The rule version the obligation comes from: what the analyst reviews.

category.description: What kind of error the reporter says it is.

description.description: The reporter's account, masked for personal identifiers before it left the obligation service: a GSTIN, PAN, Aadhaar number, phone number or email address reads as its bracketed kind, such as [PHONE].
